title: [B2 • Band 6.0] Bài 311: The Architecture of Ignorance: Rethinking Scientific Progress
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 311 (LEVEL B2 • BAND 6.0)

The Architecture of Ignorance: Rethinking Scientific Progress

Paragraph 1. In standard textbooks, scientific progress appears as a smooth, steady climb toward final truth. Each generation supposedly adds bricks onto foundations built by earlier thinkers until nature holds no secrets left. Yet in The Ignorance Ledger, philosopher of science Dr. Aris Thorne argues that this tidy story misrepresents how real discovery works. Genuine breakthroughs, Thorne insists, do not merely expand what humanity knows; their primary effect is to create entirely new forms of ignorance.

Paragraph 2. Thorne draws a clear line between 'passive ignorance' and 'strategic ignorance'. Passive ignorance is simply the absence of facts inside an untrained mind; it is static and unreflective. Strategic ignorance, by contrast, is a sophisticated state generated exclusively by major scientific advances. When physicists developed quantum mechanics in the early twentieth century, they did not tie up loose ends in classical physics; instead, they shattered Newton's predictable framework and uncovered vast mysteries regarding particle behaviour. Similarly, discovering DNA did not conclude genetics; it revealed the staggering complexities of epigenetics, proving biologists knew far less about cell control than they had once assumed.

Paragraph 3. A central target of Thorne's critique is the modern academic obsession with measuring research output through crude numbers. Funding councils, ranking boards, and grant panels judge scholars almost solely by paper counts, citation totals, and immediate commercial returns. When scientists are rewarded only for predictable outputs, they pursue 'low-risk, low-yield' tweaks—adjusting safe models rather than attempting bold inquiries that might expose deep flaws in accepted theories. Truly revolutionary projects are systematically starved of capital because their results cannot be promised on quarterly reports.

Paragraph 4. In his closing chapters, Thorne calls for a thorough reform of science teaching and funding. Rather than praising scholars who claim to possess final answers, universities should reward researchers who formulate sharper, more profound questions. By treating ignorance not as a shameful gap to conceal but as the lifeblood of inquiry, science can free itself from cautious conservatism. Science, Thorne concludes, does not conquer the darkness; it widens the boundary of the unknown.

groups.instructions: Do the following statements agree with the claims of the writer? Write YES, NO, or NOT GIVEN.

groups.title: Questions 9–12
groups.instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

q5.text: Quantum mechanics confirmed that Newton's classical framework needed no major revisions.

steps: Đoạn 2: Cơ học lượng tử đã phá vỡ khung dự đoán của Newton (shattered Newton's predictable framework).

q6.text: Most European universities have already abandoned paper counts when hiring professors.

steps: Đoạn 3: Bài chỉ nói các hội đồng hiện vẫn chấm điểm bằng số bài báo, không hề nói các trường châu Âu đã bỏ cách này.

q7.text: Advances in genetics showed that cellular regulation was more complex than earlier experts thought.

steps: Đoạn 2: Khám phá DNA mở ra epigenetics, chứng minh các nhà sinh học biết ít hơn họ tưởng.

q8.text: Academic institutions should give greater recognition to scholars who ask insightful questions.

steps: Đoạn 4: "...universities should reward researchers who formulate sharper, more profound questions."

q9.text: What is Dr. Thorne's central argument in Paragraph 1?
options: A. Modern laboratory equipment has become less accurate over time.
B. School textbooks intentionally hide ancient scientific mistakes.
C. Major scientific breakthroughs uncover brand-new categories of unknown phenomena.
D. Ordinary readers have lost interest in reading science books.

steps: Đoạn 1: Đột phá thật sự tạo ra các dạng thức chưa biết hoàn toàn mới.

q10.text: How does Thorne describe 'passive ignorance' in Paragraph 2?
options: A. As an elite tool produced by complex quantum physics
B. As an intentional refusal to read modern research papers
C. As a temporary barrier solved easily by quarterly spreadsheets
D. As a simple lack of knowledge typical of an untrained mind

steps: Đoạn 2: Sự thiếu hụt kiến thức thông thường ở một tâm trí chưa được đào tạo.

q11.text: Why does the author mention quantum mechanics in Paragraph 2?
options: A. To demonstrate that major discoveries expose limits in accepted frameworks
B. To prove that physics is mathematically simpler than biology
C. To show that Newtonian physics still explains every atomic process
D. To explain why modern physicists rarely work with biologists

steps: Đoạn 2: Cho thấy các phát kiến vĩ đại luôn bộc lộ giới hạn của hệ lý thuyết cũ.

q12.text: According to Paragraph 3, what happens when agencies rely heavily on numeric metrics?
options: A. Young scholars receive far more money than senior professors.
B. Scientists are discouraged from pursuing risky, paradigm-changing topics.
C. Academic journals stop publishing minor adjustments to safe models.
D. Universities become completely independent of corporate grants.

steps: Đoạn 3: Nhà khoa học ngại làm đề tài mạo hiểm đột phá, chỉ chạy theo dự án an toàn ít rủi ro.
